_comment: Esther's six Greek additions, in the two numberings that can be reconciled.
The additions are cited two ways. Editions following the Vulgate append them to the
end of the book as chapters 10:4-16:24; the NRSV, NABRE and most modern Catholic
editions letter them A to F and print each where the Greek puts it. Both name the
same text, so a citation in either should resolve.
A third numbering exists -- the Septuagint's, which interleaves the additions as
reconciled here. The upstream data for it is self-contradictory (see
corrections.json), and no corpus this library fetches carries it: the Swete
digitisation has only Esther's Hebrew portion, 166 verses with no additions at all,
and the World English Bible folds Additions A, B, D and E into bracketed text inside
single verses rather than numbering them. Claiming a correspondence there would be
claiming one that nothing could be checked against.
Every row below was checked against the Douay-Rheims text itself, not inferred. The
verse counts of five additions fall out exactly; the sixth is the interesting one and
is explained in its own note.
source: Douay-Rheims 1899 American Edition, as distributed by eBible.org (engDRA).

A.title: Mordecai's dream, and the plot of the two eunuchs
A.check: Vulgate 11:2-12 is eleven verses and 12:1-6 is six: seventeen, matching A:1-17. Vulgate 11:2 opens 'In the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the great, in the first day of the month Nisan, Mardochai...', which is the opening of Addition A.

B.title: The edict of Artaxerxes against the Jews

C.title: The prayers of Mordecai and of Esther
C.check: Vulgate 13:8-18 is eleven verses and 14:1-19 is nineteen: thirty, matching C:1-30.

D.title: Esther comes before the king
D.check: The one addition whose arithmetic does not fall out at a chapter boundary. Vulgate chapter 15 has nineteen verses to the letter form's sixteen, because 15:1-3 is a Vulgate doublet -- 'And he commanded her (no doubt but he was Mardochai) to go to the king, and petition for her people' recapitulates the instruction already given in 4:8, and has no counterpart in the Greek. Addition D proper begins at 15:4, 'And on the third day she laid away the garments she wore, and put on her glorious apparel', which is the Greek's opening of D. 15:4-19 is sixteen verses, matching D:1-16.

E.title: The second edict of Artaxerxes, in favour of the Jews

F.title: Mordecai's dream interpreted, and the colophon
F.check: Vulgate 10:4-13 is ten verses and 11:1 is one: eleven, matching F:1-11. Vulgate 10:4 opens 'Then Mardochai said: God hath done these things', the start of Addition F, and 11:1 is the colophon 'In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra...', which ends it.

unmatched.reason: A Vulgate doublet of the instruction at 4:8, with no counterpart in the Greek and so no letter-chapter reference. Citable in Vulgate numbering; it simply has no A-F equivalent.
